items.question: What is EmDash?
items.answer: EmDash is an Astro-native CMS with a full admin panel. You model content in the admin, and your Astro site queries it. It deploys to Cloudflare Workers or to a Node.js server.

items.question: Do I need Cloudflare to run EmDash?
items.answer: No. Cloudflare Workers with D1 and R2 is one option. EmDash also runs on Node.js with SQLite and local file storage, for example on a VPS. The EmDash review on bitdoze.com compares both.

items.question: Are the themes and plugins listed here free?
items.answer: Each listing carries a Free or Paid badge. Paid entries show the price and link to the seller's page.

items.question: Who runs this site?

data.title: EmdashHQ contact forms
data.summary: A contact form plugin for EmDash CMS. Build forms in the admin, drop them into pages with a block, store every submission in the site database, and deliver notification email through whichever email provider is already configured — Cloudflare Email Sending or any SMTP provider via emdash-smtp. The plugin never talks to an email service itself; it calls ctx.email.send(), so it works with both options and any future provider.

data.title: Stop contact form spam with Cloudflare Turnstile
data.excerpt: The contact form on this site was feeding the inbox junk. Turnstile took it to zero: here is the fifteen-minute setup, the page-cache trap we hit, and how to test it.

$media.alt: A paper mailbox behind a small turnstile gate, letters held at the checkpoint

children.text: The contact form here started collecting junk submissions. The built-in filters (honeypot field, minimum fill time, a per-IP hourly limit) stopped some of it, but enough got through to make the inbox annoying.

So the Contact Forms plugin got Cloudflare Turnstile. It runs a quiet browser check, hands the form a token, and the worker verifies that token before anything is stored or emailed. Most visitors never see a puzzle. Managed mode only escalates the suspicious ones.

body.caption: The submit pipeline: the honeypot, fill-time check and hourly limit run first, Turnstile verifies the token at the door, and only then does anything reach the inbox.

$media.alt: The submission pipeline: envelope, honey pot, clock and turnstile gate guarding the inbox

children.text: What you need

items.text: A Cloudflare account (the free plan covers Turnstile)
Contact Forms plugin 1.1.0 or newer
Two keys: the site key and the secret key
About fifteen minutes

children.text: Set it up

items.title: Create a Turnstile site
items.body: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Turnstile and choose Add site. Enter your real hostname and keep the Managed widget mode. Cloudflare shows the site key and secret key once; copy both.

items.title: Open the plugin settings
items.body: Admin → Plugins → Contact forms → Settings. The two Turnstile fields only exist on 1.1.0 and newer.

items.title: Paste both keys and save
items.body: The site key renders the widget; the secret key verifies tokens. Set only one and the plugin stays off; a half-configured pair is treated as unconfigured.

items.title: Redeploy the site
items.body: If your pages are cached, the cached HTML has no widget on it. Redeploy or purge the cache, otherwise visitors submit with no token and get bounced.

items.title: Test it
items.body: Load the form page and look for the widget, then submit once yourself to confirm the happy path still works.

body.caption: The plugin settings screen: the Turnstile site key and secret key sit next to the built-in rate limit.

$media.alt: The contact forms plugin settings page showing the Turnstile key fields

children.text: Verify it from the outside
A POST with no token should never reach the inbox. From a terminal:
You want a 303 redirect to ?cf_status=challenge. The submission is not stored and no email goes out. A real browser submit carries the cf-turnstile-response token and lands in the inbox instead.

body.caption: Submissions that pass land in the inbox with an email status for each one. Blocked posts never get a row.

$media.alt: The submissions inbox listing stored form entries with status and email columns

body.title: The cache trap we actually hit

children.text: Keys were saved, but the page showed no widget. The deploy had warmed a widget-less copy of the contact page into the Workers cache and kept serving it. A redeploy fixed it. If the widget does not appear after saving, suspect the cache before the keys.
Worth knowing

items.label: User friction
items.value: Usually invisible; Managed mode only challenges suspects

items.label: Privacy
items.value: No tracking cookies, no puzzle farm

items.title: Does it stop all spam?
items.body: It stops automated posts and most scripted junk. A determined human can still pass a challenge. If flagged submissions keep slipping through, the plugin can quarantine them: stored as spam, never emailed.

items.title: Does it work without JavaScript?
items.body: No. The widget needs JavaScript in the browser. That is the point: bots posting the raw endpoint get challenged regardless.

items.title: Where do real submissions go?
items.body: Same places as before: the admin inbox under Plugins → Contact forms, and an email through the site's configured provider.

body.caption: The live form on this site: in managed mode the widget renders nothing until Cloudflare decides a visitor needs a challenge.

$media.alt: The public contact form rendered on the site

data.title: Nineteen content widgets for EmDash posts and pages
data.excerpt: Callouts, numbered steps, tabs, code blocks, video facades and more for the block editor. What ships in the plugin, how to install it, and where to see it working.

$media.alt: A grid of small paper widget cards, accordion folds, checklists, buttons, laid out like letterpress blocks

children.text: Articles on this site needed more than paragraphs. Callouts for warnings, numbered steps for walkthroughs, code blocks for commands. The Content Widgets plugin adds nineteen block types to the EmDash editor, and they work in post bodies and on regular pages.

Everything renders on the server. There is no client-side bundle to load, and every widget picks up the site's own type scale and colors through CSS variables, so it looks like part of the theme rather than a bolt-on.

body.caption: The catalog page the plugin adds under Plugins → Content Widgets: every block with a preview, a one-line description and its type name.

$media.alt: The Content Widgets catalog in the EmDash admin

children.text: Install it

items.label: From the registry
items.body: Admin → Plugins → Browse → find Content Widgets → Install. The package is @bitdoze.com/emdashhq-widgets on plugins.emdashcms.com.

items.label: From source
items.body: Clone the plugin into your site's plugins/ directory, register it under sandboxed: in astro.config.mjs, and add it to package.json as a file: dependency. The repo has the full layout.

children.text: Allow the block types

New block types do not appear in the editor until a blocks field allows them. Open the collection, edit the blocks field, and tick the widget types under allowed types. In a seed file it looks like this:

Sandboxed plugins cannot register Astro components into a site's render pipeline, so the package ships its renderers in site/. Copy site/components into your project and map them in your blocks component; the README walks through it in four steps.

body.caption: Once the types are allowed, they show up in the block picker alongside the regular blocks.

$media.alt: A widget block picked from the EmDash post editor

data.title: How the blog on this site works
data.excerpt: A posts collection, one Astro route and a hub block. The whole thing took an afternoon, including one redirect bug worth a warning.

$media.alt: A vintage printing press feeding out a magazine page, a stack of paper beside it

children.text: This site has a blog now. Not a separate app: a posts collection, one Astro route, and a block that lists articles on the /blog page. Here is the anatomy of it, so you can build the same thing, or take it apart to see how EmDash pieces fit together.

items.label: Collection
items.value: posts: title, excerpt, cover, body blocks

body.caption: The whole blog in three pieces: the posts collection holds the data, one route renders every slug, and the body blocks become the article.

$media.alt: The blog pipeline: posts collection, one route, the rendered article

children.text: The collection

The posts collection is regular EmDash schema. The interesting bits are the urlPattern, which makes entries routable and lands them in the sitemap, and the body field, a blocks field where all the widgets live.
The route
One file renders every post. It looks the entry up by slug, rewrites to /404 when it is missing, and hands the body blocks to the widget renderer:
getSeoMeta resolves the SEO tab on each post (meta title, description, og image) and falls back to the title and excerpt when the fields are empty. Canonical and robots come along for free.
The hub page

/blog itself is an ordinary page with a site_posts block on it. The block queries the posts collection, orders by published date, and renders the card list. The page is content, not code: editors can move it, rename it and add blocks around it without touching the repo.
One trap worth knowing

Setting Astro's trailingSlash to "always" 404s every /_emdash/api/ route without a trailing slash; it briefly broke the contact form on this site. The sitemap emits slashless post URLs that 301 to the canonical form. That redirect is expected and harmless: do not try to fix it with trailingSlash.
Ship list

items.title: Do widgets work on pages too?
items.body: Yes — any blocks field can allow the widget_ types. This site allows them on pages and on posts.

items.title: What about the table of contents?
items.body: It scans the rendered h2 and h3 headings in the browser and links to them. No config needed.

items.title: Can I restyle the widgets?
items.body: Every component uses wgt- classes and falls back to plain CSS values when the site does not define the theme tokens.

items.label: npm
items.body: npm install emdashhq-widgets — then register the plugin in astro.config.mjs under sandboxed.

items.label: pnpm
items.body: pnpm add emdashhq-widgets — same registration step afterwards.

items.label: Registry
items.body: Or install from the EmDash plugin registry in the admin: Plugins, Add plugin, search Content Widgets.
